content: Has anyone gotten the comparator to work when Quot.sound is involved? I am trying to figure out whether uncaught exception: (kernel) unknown constant 'Eq' is a bug in the compartor, lean4export, or lean4checker

I've previously used comparator to check results from Mathlib so it is certainly possible yes, lean4export also manages to correctly export Quot.sound from the module based from a cursory look at its output so I would suspect that this is an issue with the replay system from lean4checker. Though also a very specific issue because only in the very minimal configurations that you use does Eq not get added through some other mean before Quot.sound pops up eventually.
CC @Kim Morrison if something in the lean4checker codebase regarding dependencies of axioms comes to mind.
Sorry, can't think of anything. I'm not sure what "the very minimal configurations that you use" is referring to, but maybe it is out of the intended scope of these tools? :-)

It very much is in scope. It refers to the very small theorem that Jason is trying to check:

theorem mp : ∀ (P Q : Prop), P → (P → Q) → Q :=
  fun _ _ hp hpq => hpq hp

Comparator will load both the theorem as well as all of the allowed axioms (including Quot.sound) and their dependencies into lean4checker. It appears that usually Eq happens to be addded before Quot.sound through some other dependency path but in this specific situation that does not end up being the case.
At least when I print both the output from lean4export and the list of declarations that comparator sends to lean4checker I can clearly see that Eq is being sent
I see. I was wondering (since Quot.sound is involved everywhere) if perhaps there was some alternative prelude being used.
Repro at https://github.com/kim-em/scratch-comparator-unknown-constant
Fix at https://github.com/leanprover/lean4checker/pull/79

Henrik Böving said:

No that is not possible. Why do you need that?

Since I already have a sandbox (docker) I'm running it in and landrun sandbox adds unnecessary complexity?

The sandbox of comparator is not meant to protect your system from malicious code. It's meant to protect itself from exploits. For example, suppose you are running in dual kernel mode with nanoda and the built-in kernel. An attacker could simply add a meta program to their file that replaces the nanoda binary with one that always says accept, thus reducing the level of trust provided by Comparator. Thus giving up on the sandboxing functionality is not really negotiatable. If anything the sandbox is still too loose.

In general, the whole architecture of Comparator is built around defense in depth. Even if you manage to find a way to break assumptions that were made during development, it should be as hard as possible to turn these issues into a functioning exploit.

Recently we have been interested in running Comparator on Math Inc.'s contributions to the Sphere Packing project. We were discouraged by Comparator's README, which starts with the assumption

Only the Solution.lean file is controlled by a potentially malicious party, all other files including most crucially lakefile.toml/lakefile.lean and Challenge.lean are controlled by you.

Since in our case the new untrusted code is ~50k lines spread over hundreds of files, that assumption feels like a non-starter.

My question now is: what guarantees do we get if we ignore this assumption? Does comparator still do a kernel check for Solution.lean and all of its dependencies?
Yes you can have an import closure of Solution.lean that is controlled by the attacker as long as it does not overlap with the import closure of your challenge of course.
I'll edit the README to make that more precise, thanks for the feedback!
OK, so if I have high confidence that my Challenge.lean states the correct theorem, then it should be okay that the solution is spread over many files?
Yes!
Is there any benefit to having the solution fit in a single file, or is that just an oversimplification in the readme?

Also my understanding was that Math Inc was already using Comparator for their work on the sphere packing project, so maybe they can clarify the usage? My assumption was that this is why their repo was structured to have separate files with MainTheorem declarations.

In practice of course the import closures of the challenge and solution will overlap (because they'll both use things from mathlib) but presumably the point is that they are allowed to overlap on files which the attacker doesn't control.

It's an underapproximation of the capabilities of comparator. The important part is that the import closure of the challenge and the lake file is not compromised such that the attacker cannot manipulate the ground truth that is extracted from the challenge file.
Yes, we saw that Math Inc was using Comparator and we wanted a better understanding of exactly what it was showing.
We had considered using Comparator on our end, but had (prematurely) given up on it, due to misunderstanding the capabilities.
That makes sense, thanks for the clarification!
Basically if you can be sure that lake build Challenge produces an olean with the contents that you want it to have everything is okay
which parts of Comparator run under the landrun sandbox?
Everything apart from the root process
Even parts of the root process could be made to run with dropped privileges but forking in Lean is hard

~/Anderson-Conjecture$ lake env comparator config.json
Building Challenge

uncaught exception: Child exited with 1

which Claude is claiming is because I'm on Linux 6.8.0 (I am) and then something about ABI 4 and ABI 5 and needing to be on 6.10 or above for landrun to work properly -- this is all beyond me. I am not able to judge the correctness of Claude's comments so thought I'd ask here.
How did you install landrun?
go install github.com/zouuup/landrun/cmd/landrun@latest

That is unfortunately only going to install the latest released version of landrun which is not good enough, we need the master version to account for this. The instructions from the repo above are correct:

# Build landrun (requires Go)
git clone https://github.com/Zouuup/landrun.git
cd landrun && go build -o landrun cmd/landrun/main.go && cd ..

Thanks -- that has solved the problem!

Update: comparator does indeed verify that the repo discussed at #AI authored projects > Rethlas+Archon Solved A Conjecture with Formal Verification @ 💬 does indeed resolve the conjecture in commutative algebra discussed there.
